sn21.10:1.2: The suffix _-nāmaka_ is a slight; see [sn10.2:1.2]() and _nāmaka_ in the sense “mere words” ([mn80:15.5](), [mn99:10.5]()). The Buddha avoids this term and just calls him “Senior”.
sn21.10:3.6: See BB’s note. I don’t get why he’s puzzled about the use of the plural form. Surely it just means “one’s own body and the bodies of others.”
